title: Credit Hold, Closure and Termination of Physician Client Accounts
content:
An account under Physician Client Accounts goes on credit hold when its oldest unpaid period has been past due for the class's credit-hold number of calendar days, or when the organization's total balance is above the class's credit limit.

## Policy

- **Placing the hold.** An account goes on credit hold when its oldest unpaid period is the class's credit-hold number of calendar days past due, or when the organization's total balance exceeds the class's credit limit. Days past due are counted, as of today, in calendar days since the due date of the oldest client invoice period that still has an unpaid amount. The hold is placed automatically and its start date is recorded on the account.
- **Releasing the hold.** The hold is released when every past-due amount is paid (every class requires the full past-due amount for release) and the balance is back within the limit. The release is automatic, and the earlier credit-hold date is kept on the account as history.
- **Closure for nonpayment.** An account left on credit hold more than the class's closure number of calendar days may be closed by the laboratory.
- **Termination by the organization.** The organization ends its agreement with the class's termination-notice number of calendar days of written notice. Only the organization can terminate, and the final client invoice still falls due.

## Status movements

| From | To | Brought about by | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| Active | Credit hold | The system | The oldest unpaid period reaches the credit-hold point in days past due, or the organization's total balance exceeds the credit limit |
| Credit hold | Active | The system | Every past-due amount is paid and the balance is within the credit limit |
| Active | Closed | The organization | It terminates the client agreement with the required written notice |
| Credit hold | Closed | The laboratory | The account has been on credit hold more than the closure number of days |

## Casebook (hypothetical accounts; the figures 60 and 90 are example inputs)

- **Days past due run from the oldest unpaid period.** An account's oldest unpaid period fell due on 31 March, and later periods are paid. With a credit-hold point of 60 days, that period is 59 days past due on 29 May and 60 days past due on 30 May, when the hold applies.
- **Balance above the limit.** An organization whose total balance across its open accounts is above its class's credit limit has its accounts placed on credit hold, even with no period yet at the days-past-due point.
- **Release.** An account on hold whose past-due amounts are all paid and whose organization balance is back within the limit is released. An account on hold with any past-due amount still unpaid stays on hold.
- **Closure.** With a closure figure of 90 days, an account that has been on credit hold for 90 calendar days has not yet been on hold more than 90; at 91 days the laboratory may close it.
- **Termination.** An organization that gives its written notice of termination still owes the final client invoice when it falls due.
